text:
maria: CI failing on infra/gpu-cluster repo — GH Actions runs keep getting stuck waiting for locks and then helm times out. Seen this across 3 runs in the last hour. Any idea what changed?

sam: I saw the same. Logs show GHA concurrency holds the job but two runs end up trying to provision GPUs at once which trips cloud quota and then terraform hangs on apply.

maria: snippet from the runner logs: ```
[2026-02-23T10:12:03Z] Waiting to acquire lock: dynamodb-lock-table, attempt=1
[2026-02-23T10:12:33Z] Acquired lock, running terraform apply
[2026-02-23T10:15:40Z] Error: API quota exceeded: Max GPU cores per region reached
[2026-02-23T10:20:00Z] helm upgrade --install gpu-stack ./charts/gpu --timeout 300s --wait 
Error: Timed out waiting for resources: pods/gpu-provisioner not ready
```

alex: FWIW we recently turned on parallel helm/terraform in the workflow to shorten rollout time. That lets separate PRs hit infra at the same time. Concurrency group is set to `infra-apply-${{ github.ref }}` so it only cancels identical branches, not concurrent PRs against main.

jen: That explains it — parallel runs are racing to create node pools. AWS quota and cloudprovider rate limits cause partial applies and terraform ends up with state drift. We saw extra orphaned instances yesterday.

sam: Two immediate ideas: 1) tighten concurrency group to a global lock e.g. `concurrency: group: infra-apply-global` with `cancel-in-progress: false` so runs queue. 2) Add a pre-check step to fail fast if quota is insufficient (call cloud API to check available GPU quota).

maria: Agree. Also, is our terraform backend locking reliable? We're using s3 + dynamodb for locking — logs show we sometimes get a transient 'lock lost' message from the runner (maybe network blip). Could be GHA runner flapping makes the lock not released neatly.

infra-oncall: We just did a manual reconcile: `terraform state list | grep module.gpu` and then `terraform apply -target=module.gpu_pool -auto-approve` from a stable runner in our control plane. That unblocked routing, but left a partial helm release that needed `helm rollback`.

alex: For longer-term: add a per-repo mutex action (e.g. actions/cache-based mutex or peter-evans/lock) + quota pre-check + revert the parallelism change for gpu stacks. We can still parallelize low-risk changes.

jen: Also consider switching terraform to use `-refresh=false` during plan in CI and require a separate gated apply job that runs serially against main. Keeps plans fast and ensures only one apply mutates infra.

sam: +1. We should also increase timeout for helm or split the chart so control-plane pieces come up before gpu provisioner. That reduces 300s timeout flakiness.

maria: Quick patch I pushed to the workflow: changed concurrency to `infra-apply-global`, added a `preflight-gpu-quota-check` step that calls our quota-check lambda, and set `cancel-in-progress: false`. Will monitor.

gha-bot: GitHub Actions: workflow `infra-apply` triggered on push to main by maria — run queued (id: 4321).

infra-oncall: FYI we should open a ticket to audit remaining repos that enabled parallel infra applies. I can do that and create a playbook for manual reconcile (commands, where to run, rollback steps).

maria: Thanks — can you create the ticket and link here? Also let's add a short runbook to the repo about 'if quota exceeded, do X then Y'.

jen: I'll draft a RFC for gating applies and the layout of serial apply runners. Want to include metrics: average apply duration, failure rate, and quota checks.

sam: For now, if you see a stuck job, don't approve a new run — wait for the queued one. And if we need emergency capacity, use the oncall-runner with manual lock.

maria: Good plan. I'll keep monitoring and drop updates here. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
